newSources.title: The original Doom cheat handler
newSources.scope: Developer-released source identifies the classic cheat sequences, their effects and the single-player/non-Nightmare restriction. Linux source released in 1997, not instructions for modern console ports.

newSources.title: Gran Turismo: English software manual, pp. 14–15
newSources.scope: Original manual: game data occupies five blocks, replay data a separate file; one game-data file per card. Archived scan.

newSources.title: Final Fantasy VII: original packaging and variants
newSources.publisher: Sony Computer Entertainment America; scans catalogued by Game-Rave
newSources.scope: SCUS-94163 packaging identifies one memory-card block per save. The packaging is primary evidence; collector commentary is secondary.

newSources.title: PlayStation Underground 1.1: disc menus and packaging
newSources.publisher: Sony Computer Entertainment America; preserved by Game-Rave
newSources.scope: Primary menu/packaging scans for the 1997 US two-disc set SCUS-94161, PSRM-006590/006600. Shows Vault, Download Station and disc-two playable/video contents.

newSources.title: Pete Rock on finding “Today”
newSources.publisher: Bullseye with Jesse Thorn / Maximum Fun
newSources.scope: Producer interview transcript: Tom Scott’s Today and the making of They Reminisce Over You. Does not identify the pictured MPC2000 as its production equipment.

newSources.title: My Life: recordings and artist commentary
newSources.scope: Album track sequence and durations; Roy Ayers source for My Life and Curtis Mayfield source for Be Happy. Listening commentary here is original.

newSources.title: In the beginning, there was Shy FX
newSources.publisher: Shy FX interviewed by Ian McQuaid, TRENCH
newSources.scope: Producer’s account of making Original Nuttah with UK Apache, Amen editing and the tension between complexity and dancefloor groove.

newSources.title: The musicians behind the Amen break
newSources.scope: Interview with Winstons bandleader Richard Spencer about Amen, Brother and the sampled drum break.

newSources.title: Fabio selects drum & bass records
newSources.scope: Participant listening commentary explicitly identifies the Amen break in Original Nuttah; interview rather than a generic genre history.

newSources.title: Blue Lines: identified 2012 mix/master
newSources.scope: Official distributed album tracklist, performer credits and durations. Reissue timings are used explicitly; no day-level 1991 release claim is inferred.

newSources.title: Dummy: album and track timings
newSources.publisher: Go! Discs / Island Records / Apple Music
newSources.scope: Distributed album recordings, track sequence and timings, including Sour Times 4:12 and Roads 5:03. Storefront date fields are not used as release dates.

newSources.title: Maxinquaye: Reincarnated, disc one
newSources.scope: 2023 Abbey Road remaster of the 1995 album. Identifies Martina Topley-Bird and Hell Is Round The Corner at 3:47. Used as an explicitly modern reference version.

newSources.title: CrazySexyCool and TLC recordings
newSources.scope: Artist catalogue and recordings establish named 1994 and 1999 album examples. Vocal descriptions are original listening notes.

newSources.title: September 1998 daily TRL recaps
newSources.scope: Retrospective fan-maintained transcript archive, reposted in 2020, supplies September 14, 1998 top ten. Not an official MTV voting record; provenance is stated in the story.

newSources.title: CSS support in MS IE 3.0, updated September 1, 1996
newSources.scope: Contemporary CSS demonstrations and implementation limitations: missing padding, border properties and em units. Windows-era IE3 comparison; not modern browser behavior.

newSources.title: The CSS saga
newSources.publisher: Håkon Wium Lie and Bert Bos / W3C
newSources.scope: CSS authors trace IE3 support in 1996 and Navigator 4 support later. Navigator 3 is not presented as a CSS browser.

newSources.title: Internet Explorer 3.0 for Windows 3.1 announcement
newSources.scope: Platform-specific announcement lists frames and scripting support. Used to distinguish the December Windows 3.1 release from August’s Windows 95 version.

newSources.title: Electronic Furby instruction manual, 708000001IWT1-07
newSources.publisher: Tiger Electronics, 1999 printing; preserved by The Old Robots
newSources.scope: Original-generation manual: four AA batteries, touch/light/sound/orientation sensors, feeding switch, progressive language behavior and interaction with other Furbys. Not a 2005, 2012 or 2023 model.

newSources.title: Original Tamagotchi: Generation 1 programming
newSources.scope: Current rerelease explicitly preserves 1997 programming: care icons, food, health, lights, game and discipline. Contemporary shell and battery specification are not assigned to the 1997 hardware.

newSources.title: Original Tamagotchi: Generation 2 programming
newSources.scope: Bandai describes the retained Gen 2 number-comparison game, distinguishing it from the Gen 1 direction-guessing game. Current rerelease, not a period product photograph.

newSources.title: Nickelodeon announces Saturday-night lineup
newSources.scope: Contemporary announcement of 8–10 p.m. SNICK schedule. Read alongside the opening-day coverage and existing historical schedule source; regional cable carriage can vary.

newSources.title: Baduizm: original album and singles
newSources.scope: Label catalogue establishes Baduizm as a 1997 album with On & On and Next Lifetime. Listening analysis is original.

newSources.title: MZ-1 operating instructions
newSources.publisher: Sony, original manual preserved by MiniDisc.org
newSources.scope: Original model’s recording inputs and edit operations: Combine, Divide, Swap, Erase, Erase All and Label. MZ-1 is a real-time recorder; later Net MD/MDLP features are not assigned to it.

newSources.title: Game Gear: US box and manual
newSources.scope: Period packaging specifies six AA batteries and optional power accessories. Not an estimate of battery life.

newSources.title: Super Mario 64 instruction booklet
newSources.scope: Original Nintendo 64 instructions distinguish control-stick movement from C-button camera controls and explain Lakitu. Not the DS remake.

newSources.title: Casio QV-10 historical designation
newSources.scope: Maker identifies the QV-10 as a 1995 consumer digital camera with a color LCD for reviewing captured images. Does not date every pictured later camera.

newSources.title: The original 100 MB Zip system
newSources.scope: Museum technical history and manufacturer history establish the original Zip capacity and its separate drive/cartridge format.

newSources.title: Ultim8, September 25, 1992: reverse of flyer
newSources.publisher: Ultim8 / TUR Promotions; scan by Upthebuffer
newSources.scope: Primary printed invitation identifies Knighton Community Centre, the date, 8.30–1.30, £6 admission, Donovan Bad Boy Smith, Atomix, Chancey, Fizz and M.C. KRE-8. Bottom panel explicitly advertises future names.

newSources.title: El Con Mall: surviving directory
newSources.scope: Primary map identifies anchors, AMC El Con Six and The Pavilion Food Court. Described as a 1990s map by uploader, photographed in 2009; no exact printing year inferred.

newSources.title: Doom game modes in the developer source
newSources.scope: Developer’s definitions distinguish shareware’s first episode from the three-episode registered game. Original PC editions; later Ultimate Doom has additional content.

newSources.title: TB-303 Bass Line owner’s manual
newSources.scope: Original instrument’s pitch/time programming, accent, slide and tone controls. Not the TB-03, TB-3 or software emulation.

newSources.title: M1 synthesizer/workstation
newSources.scope: Maker describes the original 1988 keyboard, PCM-based synthesis, effects and eight-track sequencer. Software reissue expansions are not assigned to original hardware.

newSources.title: PalmPilot Professional handbook
newSources.scope: Original handbook documents Graffiti character input, organizer applications, cradle/HotSync and backup restoration. Not an integrated mobile phone.

newSources.title: D-121 operating instructions
newSources.scope: Model-specific portable CD-player instructions; playback controls and compatible power arrangements. No universal battery-life or skip-protection claim.

newSources.title: WM-FX151 operating instructions
newSources.scope: Identified cassette Walkman and radio model. Playback controls, tape direction and power are described without adding recording or later digital transfer features.

newSources.title: PlayStation Underground Jampack: 1998 packaging and contents
newSources.publisher: Sony Computer Entertainment America; preserved by Game-Rave
newSources.scope: Primary sleeve and disc evidence identifies SCUS-94287 / PSRM-010560. Eight advertised playable demos include Gran Turismo, Tekken 3 and Tomba!; video previews and imports have separate listings.

newSources.title: Large Professor on digging for records
newSources.publisher: Large Professor interviewed by Chairman Mao / Red Bull Music Academy
newSources.scope: Producer describes buying records in the Village and Bleecker Records near House of Oldies, plus the Tom Scott record. Interview evidence for a specific independent-shop route.

newSources.title: Bladder water-gun mechanism
newSources.scope: Primary technical disclosure of a pump, reservoir and expandable elastic bladder. Supports the mechanism family, not an exact performance or range claim for an individual retail specimen.
